This endpoint handles the first step of the "Forgot Password" self-service recovery mechanism. When users provide their email address, the system validates the email exists in todo_list_users and the account is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null). A cryptographically secure random token is generated, stored in the todo_list_password_reset_tokens table with a 1-hour expiration (expires_at set to created_at + 1 hour), and sent to the user's email address.

The generated token must be unique across all active tokens to prevent collisions, enforced by the unique index on the token field. The system stores both the token and the email address for validation, providing an additional security layer during the password reset completion. Multiple tokens can exist for the same user if they request password reset multiple times before using a token.

The password reset email contains a secure link with the token embedded, directing users to the password reset completion page. This public endpoint does not require authentication since users have lost access to their accounts. For security, the endpoint should not reveal whether an email exists in the system to prevent email enumeration attacks.

The token creation follows strict security controls: tokens expire after 1 hour (enforced through expires_at validation), are single-use only (tracked through used_at field), and are permanently deleted after successful password reset or expiration. This implements industry-standard password recovery while maintaining strict security requirements.

This endpoint handles the second step of the password reset flow after users click the reset link from their email. The system validates the provided token exists in todo_list_password_reset_tokens, hasn't expired (current time < expires_at), hasn't been used (used_at is null), and matches the provided email address for additional security verification.

Upon successful token validation, the system updates the password_hash field in todo_list_users with the new password securely hashed using bcrypt with cost factor of at least 12. The updated_at timestamp is automatically updated to reflect the password change. The token's used_at field is set to the current timestamp, permanently preventing token reuse and enforcing the single-use security requirement.

As a security measure, successful password reset triggers invalidation of all active sessions for the user by setting expired_at on all records in todo_list_user_sessions. This implements a "logout from all devices" behavior, ensuring that if an unauthorized party gained access, they are immediately logged out when the legitimate user resets their password.

Password reset failures occur when the token is not found, has expired based on the expires_at timestamp, has already been used (used_at is not null), or when the email doesn't match the token's stored email. The system enforces strict token expiration through the 1-hour limit set during token creation, and tokens are permanently deleted after successful use or expiration.

This completes the self-service password recovery mechanism, allowing users to regain access to their accounts securely while maintaining strict security controls through time-limited, single-use tokens and automatic session invalidation.

This prevents unauthorized password changes if someone gains temporary access to an authenticated session.

The system validates the current password against the stored password_hash in todo_list_users using bcrypt verification before allowing the change. Upon successful verification, the password_hash field is updated with the new password securely hashed using bcrypt with cost factor of at least 12. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set to reflect the password modification.

As a security best practice, successful password change triggers invalidation of all other active sessions for the user by setting expired_at on all records in todo_list_user_sessions except the current session. This implements a "logout from all other devices" behavior, ensuring that if an unauthorized party gained access on another device, they are immediately logged out when the user changes their password.

This operation maintains the current session's validity, allowing the user to continue working after the password change without requiring re-authentication. The user receives confirmation of the successful password update and should be advised that all other devices were logged out for security.

Password change failures occur when the current password verification fails, when the new password doesn't meet security requirements, or when the user account has been soft-deleted. This endpoint requires authentication through JWT token validation and can only be accessed by the account owner.

The operation enforces strict ownership validation - only the user who created the todo (matched via todo_list_user_id foreign key) can delete it. ITodoListGuest.ICreate.description:
Guest user registration request data for creating a new account in the todo_list_users table.

This schema represents the information required from a user during the registration process. It captures the essential credentials, optional profile information, and session context metadata needed to create a new guest account with immediate session establishment.

The email field serves as the unique identifier for authentication and must conform to standard email format validation. The password field accepts the user's plain-text password, which the backend will hash using bcrypt before storing in the password_hash column of the todo_list_users table.

The optional name field allows users to provide a display name for personalization purposes. Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are included to enable immediate session creation in the todo_list_user_sessions table upon successful registration, providing audit trail and security monitoring capabilities.

All timestamp fields (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are system-managed and excluded from this creation request. Security considerations: The password is transmitted in plain text over HTTPS and immediately hashed server-side. The email uniqueness is enforced by database constraints to prevent duplicate accounts.

email.description:
User's email address for authentication and communication.

Must be unique across all users in the todo_list_users table. This field serves as the primary login identifier and is validated against RFC 5322 email format standards.

The database enforces uniqueness through an index constraint, preventing duplicate registrations with the same email address.

password.description:
User's password in plain text format for account security.

This password will be cryptographically hashed using bcrypt with a cost factor of at least 12 before being stored in the password_hash field of the database. The plain text password is never stored.

Password strength requirements should include minimum length of 8 characters. The client should enforce additional complexity requirements as needed.

name.description:
Optional display name for the guest user account.

This field provides a human-friendly identifier for personalization purposes. If not provided, the system may use the email address or a default placeholder for display purposes.

The name can be updated later through profile management endpoints.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring.

This optional field captures the IP address from which the guest registration request originates. While the server can extract this from the HTTP request headers, clients may provide it explicitly for server-side rendering scenarios.

The IP address is stored in the todo_list_user_sessions table as part of the session record created during registration. It supports audit trails, security monitoring, and helps detect suspicious account creation patterns.

Both IPv4 and IPv6 address formats are supported. If not provided by the client, the backend will extract it from the request context.

href.description:
Connection URL indicating the current page from which registration was initiated.

This required field captures the full URL of the page where the guest user submitted their registration request. It represents the connection context at the moment of account creation.

The href value is stored in the todo_list_user_sessions table as part of the initial session record. This information supports user behavior analysis, conversion tracking, and security auditing by showing the exact entry point for new guest registrations.

Must be a valid URI format. Examples include application page URLs, landing pages, or registration form locations.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating the previous page before the registration page.

This required field captures the URL of the page that led the user to the registration form. It represents the navigation context that brought the guest to the sign-up process.

The referrer value is stored in the todo_list_user_sessions table as part of the initial session record. This supports marketing attribution, user journey analysis, and helps understand how guests discover and access the registration functionality.

Must be a valid URI format. Can be an empty string for direct navigation (when users directly access the registration page without a referrer).

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token request for renewing JWT access tokens.

Contains the refresh token that was issued during the initial login or previous refresh operation. This DTO is used to request a new pair of access and refresh tokens without requiring the user to re-enter their credentials.

The refresh token must be valid, non-expired, and associated with an active session in the todo_list_user_sessions table. The session must belong to a non-deleted user account (deleted_at is null in todo_list_users).

This enables continuous authenticated access across the configured session timeout period (7 days for standard sessions, 30 days for "Remember Me" sessions).

refresh_token.description:
Valid refresh token from previous authentication.

The JWT refresh token that was issued during login or the last successful refresh operation. This token is validated against active sessions in todo_list_user_sessions to ensure it hasn't expired and belongs to a valid user account.

Must be a properly formatted JWT token. The system validates this token's signature, expiration, and association with an active session before issuing new tokens.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetRequest.description:
Password reset request containing user's email address.

Used to initiate the password recovery workflow. The provided email is validated against todo_list_users to ensure the account exists and is not deleted (deleted_at is null).

If the email exists, a cryptographically secure token is generated and stored in todo_list_password_reset_tokens with a 1-hour expiration. The token is sent via email to enable secure password reset completion.

For security, this endpoint does not reveal whether an email exists in the system to prevent email enumeration attacks.

email.description:
Email address for password reset request.

The email address associated with the user account requiring password reset. This must be a valid email format and should correspond to an existing, non-deleted account in the todo_list_users table.

If the email exists, a password reset token will be generated and sent to this address. The system validates email format but does not disclose whether the email exists to prevent account enumeration.

message.description:
Confirmation message indicating that if the email exists in the system, a password reset link has been sent.

This message uses intentionally vague wording to prevent email enumeration attacks. The system does not reveal whether the provided email address exists in todo_list_users, maintaining security by not disclosing user account existence to potential attackers.

Typical value: 'If an account with that email exists, a password reset link has been sent.'

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetRequestRespo.description:
Response confirming password reset email was sent if the email exists in the system.

This response type implements a security-first design by providing a generic success message regardless of whether the email address actually exists in todo_list_users. This prevents email enumeration attacks where malicious actors could discover valid user accounts by observing different responses for existing vs. non-existing emails.

The response is returned after the system has attempted to create a token in todo_list_password_reset_tokens and send the password reset email. If the email exists and the account is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null), a cryptographically secure token with 1-hour expiration is created and sent via email. If the email doesn't exist, the same generic message is returned without any token creation.

This consistent response pattern ensures attackers cannot determine which email addresses are registered in the system, maintaining user privacy and security while still providing a clear confirmation message to legitimate users attempting password recovery.

token.description:
Password reset token from the email link sent to the user.

This token was generated during the password reset request and stored in todo_list_password_reset_tokens. The system validates that this token exists, hasn't expired (current time < expires_at), hasn't been used (used_at is null), and matches the provided email address.

Tokens are single-use only and expire after 1 hour from creation for security.

email.description:
Email address of the user resetting their password.

Provided as an additional security verification measure to ensure the token matches the intended user account. The system validates that this email matches the email stored with the token in todo_list_password_reset_tokens.

This prevents token hijacking scenarios where an attacker might obtain a valid token but doesn't know the associated email address.

new_password.description:
New password to set for the user account.

This password will be securely hashed using bcrypt with cost factor of at least 12 before being stored in the password_hash field of todo_list_users. The plain text password is never stored.

Must meet minimum security requirements including at least 8 characters in length. Upon successful password reset, all active user sessions are invalidated for security.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetComplete.description:
Request body for completing password reset using a validated token.

This DTO handles the second step of the password reset flow where users provide the token they received via email along with their new password. The system validates the token's existence, expiration status, usage status, and email match before updating the password.

Successful password reset triggers automatic invalidation of all active sessions for the user, implementing a logout from all devices security measure.

success.description:
Indicates whether the password reset was completed successfully.

When true, the user's password has been updated in todo_list_users, the token has been marked as used in todo_list_password_reset_tokens, and all active sessions have been invalidated.

When false, the password reset failed due to invalid token, expired token, already-used token, or email mismatch.

message.description:
Human-readable message describing the result of the password reset operation.

For successful resets, confirms that the password has been updated and all devices have been logged out. For failures, provides specific information about why the reset failed (invalid token, expired token, already used, or email mismatch).

This message can be displayed to users to inform them of the outcome and any necessary next steps.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetCompleteResp.description:
Response confirming successful password reset completion.

Returned after validating the reset token and updating the user's password in todo_list_users. Indicates whether the operation succeeded and provides a descriptive message.

Successful responses confirm that the password was updated, the token was marked as used, and all active sessions were invalidated for security.

current_password.description:
Current password for verification before allowing the change.

The system validates this against the stored password_hash in todo_list_users using bcrypt verification. This prevents unauthorized password changes if someone gains temporary access to an authenticated session.

Password change will only proceed if this current password verification succeeds.

new_password.description:
New password to set for the authenticated user account.

This password will be securely hashed using bcrypt with cost factor of at least 12 before being stored in the password_hash field of todo_list_users. The plain text password is never stored.

Must meet minimum security requirements including at least 8 characters in length. Upon successful password change, all other active sessions (except the current one) are invalidated for security.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordChange.description:
Request body for authenticated users to change their password.

This DTO handles proactive password updates for users who have access to their accounts. Unlike password reset which is for account recovery, password change requires authentication and current password verification.

Successful password change invalidates all other sessions except the current one, implementing a logout from all other devices security measure while maintaining the current session.

success.description:
Indicates whether the password change operation completed successfully.

This field confirms that the user's current password was verified correctly, the new password met all security requirements, and the password_hash field in todo_list_users was updated successfully.

A true value means the password has been changed and all other active sessions in todo_list_user_sessions have been invalidated for security purposes.

message.description:
Human-readable confirmation message describing the password change result.

Provides clear feedback to the user about the operation outcome, typically confirming successful password update and informing that other active sessions have been logged out for security.

Example messages include 'Password changed successfully. All other devices have been logged out for security.' or similar user-friendly confirmations.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordChangeResponse.description:
Response confirming successful password change operation for authenticated user.

This response type is returned after a user successfully changes their password through the password change endpoint. It confirms that the current password was verified, the new password was securely hashed and stored in the todo_list_users table, and all other active sessions were invalidated for security.

The response provides clear confirmation to the user that their password has been updated and informs them about the security measure of logging out all other devices. This helps users understand that if they had logged in on multiple devices, they will need to re-authenticate on those other devices using the new password.

This is distinct from password reset responses, as password change requires current password verification and is performed by authenticated users proactively updating their credentials.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Determines which page of results to retrieve from the filtered user list. Combined with limit to calculate the offset for database queries.

Defaults to 1 if not specified, showing the first page of results.

limit.description:
Number of user records to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination results. Maximum value is enforced at 100 to prevent excessive data retrieval and maintain system performance.

Defaults to a reasonable value (typically 20-50) if not specified. Larger limits may impact response time for queries with complex filters.

search.description:
Full-text search query for filtering users by email or name.

Performs partial matching across both the email and name fields in todo_list_users table. The search is case-insensitive and matches any portion of the email address or display name.

For example, searching 'john' would match users with email 'john@example.com', 'johndoe@domain.com', or name 'John Smith'. This enables flexible user discovery without requiring exact matches.

email.description:
Filter users by exact or partial email address match.

Searches the email field in todo_list_users table for matches. Supports partial matching to find users with similar email addresses or from specific domains.

Email filtering is case-insensitive and can be used to locate users by their registered email address, which serves as the unique identifier for authentication.

name.description:
Filter users by display name with partial matching.

Searches the name field in todo_list_users table for matches. The name is an optional field that users can set for personalization, so this filter may not match users who haven't set a display name.

Partial matching is case-insensitive, allowing flexible search across user display names.

created_at_start.description:
Start date for filtering users by account creation date (inclusive).

Filters for users whose created_at timestamp in todo_list_users is on or after this date. Must be in ISO 8601 date-time format.

Used in conjunction with created_at_end to define a date range for registration queries. For example, to find all users who registered during a specific month or quarter.

created_at_end.description:
End date for filtering users by account creation date (inclusive).

Filters for users whose created_at timestamp in todo_list_users is on or before this date. Must be in ISO 8601 date-time format.

Combined with created_at_start to create bounded date ranges for finding users registered within specific time periods.

include_deleted.description:
Flag to include soft-deleted user accounts in search results.

When set to true, results will include users with a non-null deleted_at timestamp in todo_list_users, showing both active and soft-deleted accounts.

Defaults to false, returning only active users. Including deleted users is useful for administrative reviews, account recovery within the 30-day soft delete period, or audit purposes.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort the user list results by.

Determines the ordering criterion for the returned user records. Available options correspond to key fields in the todo_list_users table.

Defaults to 'created_at' when not specified, showing newest user registrations first. Sorting by email provides alphabetical user listing, while sorting by name orders by display name (users without names may appear first or last depending on implementation).

ITodoListUser.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for querying user accounts with pagination support.

This request DTO provides comprehensive filtering capabilities for browsing and searching user accounts in the todo_list_users table. All filter parameters are optional, allowing queries ranging from retrieving all users (with pagination) to highly specific searches based on multiple criteria.

The search functionality supports both broad queries (using the search parameter for full-text matching) and precise filtering (using specific field filters like email or name). Date range filtering enables administrative queries for user registration analytics or time-based account management.

Pagination is implemented through the page and limit parameters, ensuring efficient handling of large user datasets. The sort_by and sort_order parameters provide flexible result ordering to support different use cases such as chronological listings, alphabetical directories, or custom sorting requirements.

Security considerations are built into the operation - this request type is used with endpoints that enforce strict authorization, ensuring only authenticated users with appropriate permissions can query user account information. The response excludes sensitive authentication data regardless of the query parameters.

This request DTO is designed for administrative user management, user directory browsing, and account search functionality within the todo list application.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the user account.

This UUID serves as the primary key in the todo_list_users table and uniquely identifies each user account across the entire application. Generated automatically upon user registration using UUID v4 format.

Used for referencing users in relationships with other entities like todos, sessions, and password reset tokens.

email.description:
User email address for authentication and communication.

Must be unique across all users in the todo_list_users table and serves as the login identifier. This field is validated for proper email format and used for account recovery.

The email address is immutable after registration to maintain authentication consistency and audit trail integrity.

name.description:
User's display name for personalization, or null if not set.

Optional field that users can provide during registration or update later. Used in welcome messages and user interface personalization throughout the application.

When null, the application may fall back to displaying the email address or a default placeholder. Maximum length of 100 characters enforced for display consistency.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the user account was created during registration.

Immutable after creation and used for account age tracking and audit purposes. This field enables chronological sorting in user lists and provides context for when users joined the system.

Displayed in ISO 8601 date-time format. Useful for administrative oversight, user analytics, and displaying account creation dates in list views.

ITodoListUser.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary of user account for list views and reference contexts.

Provides essential user identification with account creation timestamp for chronological context. Used when embedding user references in other entities like todos, password reset tokens, or categories, as well as in paginated user list responses.

This summary variant is optimized for list views and relational contexts where full user details are not needed. Excludes password hash for security, omits updated_at to minimize payload size while retaining created_at for valuable chronological information.

The field set balances completeness with efficiency, ensuring user summaries provide sufficient context without overwhelming response payloads in bulk operations or nested references.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the user account.

Primary key that uniquely identifies each user in the system. Generated automatically upon registration using UUID v4 format to ensure global uniqueness.

email.description:
User email address for authentication and communication.

Serves as the unique login identifier and primary contact method. Must be unique across all users and conform to RFC 5322 email format standards. Used for account recovery and system notifications.

name.description:
User's display name for personalization.

Optional field that can be provided during registration or updated later through profile settings. Used in welcome messages, user interface personalization, and display contexts. Maximum 100 characters.

Null when the user has not provided a display name.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the user account was created during registration.

Immutable ISO 8601 formatted timestamp recording the exact moment of account creation. Used for account age tracking, analytics, and audit purposes. Never modified after initial creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last modification to user profile information.

Automatically updated in ISO 8601 format whenever email, password, or name fields are changed. Tracks most recent account activity for security monitoring and audit trails.

deleted_at.description:
Soft delete timestamp indicating when user requested account deletion.

Null for active accounts. When set to a timestamp, the account enters a 30-day recovery period before permanent deletion. Supports account recovery requests and data retention policy compliance.

During the recovery window, the account is inaccessible but can be restored.

ITodoListUser.description:
Authenticated user account entity for the Todo list application.

Represents core user identity and authentication credentials for individuals who register and use the system. Each user account provides complete data isolation, ensuring users can only access their own todo items and personal information.

Supports the complete user lifecycle from registration through active use to optional deletion with a 30-day soft delete recovery period. The system maintains strict authentication and authorization to prevent any cross-user data access.

email.description: Updated email address. Must be unique across all users. Changing email may require re-authentication.

name.description: Updated display name. Set to null to clear existing name. Maximum 100 characters.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating user profile information.

All fields are optional for partial updates. Password changes should use a dedicated password change endpoint, not this general update operation, to ensure proper security validation.

The updated_at timestamp is automatically set by the system. Users can only update their own profile as enforced by authentication context.

id.description:
Primary unique identifier for the session record.

Generated automatically when session is created during login. Used for session management and revocation operations.

user.description:
User who owns this authentication session.

Reference to the authenticated user account. Provides user context for session tracking and audit purposes.

ip.description:
IP address from which the user connected.

Recorded during login for security monitoring and detecting suspicious login patterns from unusual locations. Used in security audit logs and anomaly detection.

href.description:
Connection URL where the session was initiated.

Captures the full URL of the login request for audit and debugging purposes. Helps trace user navigation patterns and login context.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating login source.

Indicates where the user came from before logging in. Used for tracking user acquisition sources and navigation patterns leading to authentication.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the session was created during login.

Marks the beginning of the authenticated session period. Used for session age tracking and enforcing timeout policies.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session expired or was terminated.

Null for active sessions. Set upon logout, password change, or automatic expiration after configured timeout period (7-30 days).

Once set, the session is considered invalid and associated JWT tokens should be rejected.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
User authentication session for JWT token and access tracking.

Records active user sessions for authenticated access to the application. Each session represents a login instance from a specific device or browser, tracking connection context and lifecycle.

Supports multiple concurrent sessions per user, allowing login from different devices simultaneously. Sessions can be individually revoked through logout or bulk revoked when user changes password.

Used for audit tracing of user actions and maintaining secure authentication state through JWT refresh token management.

id.description: Session identifier for reference and revocation operations.

ip.description:
IP address from which the session was created.

Displayed in session management interfaces for security monitoring.

created_at.description:
When the session was created.

Helps users identify and manage their active sessions by login time.

expired_at.description:
When the session expired or was terminated.

Null for currently active sessions. Helps distinguish active from inactive sessions.

ITodoListUserSession.ISummary.description:
Lightweight session summary for session management views.

Provides essential session information for displaying in active session lists and security management interfaces. Excludes full user object and detailed connection context for efficiency.

Used when showing users their active sessions for security monitoring and selective logout functionality.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve from the total result set. Combined with limit to calculate the offset for database queries. Defaults to 1 if not specified.

limit.description:
Number of sessions per page.

Controls the page size for pagination results. Maximum value of 100 prevents excessive data transfer and maintains reasonable response times. Defaults to 20 if not specified.

sort.description:
Sorting criteria for session results.

Array of sort specifications where each item combines direction prefix ('+' ascending, '-' descending) with field name. For example, ['-created_at', '+ip'] sorts by creation date descending, then IP ascending.

Supported fields: created_at (session creation time), expired_at (expiration time), ip (IP address). Most common use case is sorting by created_at descending to show newest sessions first.

ip.description:
Filter sessions by IP address.

Exact match filter for finding all sessions created from a specific IP address. Useful for identifying all logins from a particular location or network. Supports both IPv4 and IPv6 address formats.

created_after.description:
Filter sessions created after specified timestamp.

Inclusive lower bound for created_at filtering in ISO 8601 format. Returns sessions where created_at >= created_after. Useful for finding recent sessions or sessions within a specific time range when combined with created_before.

created_before.description:
Filter sessions created before specified timestamp.

Inclusive upper bound for created_at filtering in ISO 8601 format. Returns sessions where created_at <= created_before. Useful for historical session queries or defining time ranges when combined with created_after.

is_active.description:
Filter by session active status.

When true, returns only active sessions (expired_at is null). When false, returns only expired/terminated sessions (expired_at is not null). When null or omitted, returns all sessions regardless of status. Essential for 'show active sessions only' functionality.

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching and filtering user session lists.

Provides comprehensive filtering, sorting, and pagination capabilities for retrieving user sessions. Supports multiple filter criteria that can be combined to narrow down results, such as IP address filtering, date range queries, and active status filtering.

Pagination parameters control the page size and which page to retrieve, enabling efficient browsing of large session histories. Sorting options allow ordering by creation date, expiration date, or IP address in ascending or descending order.

All filter parameters are optional - when omitted, that filter is not applied. Multiple filters combine with AND logic to progressively narrow the result set.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the password reset token.

Primary key that uniquely identifies each password reset request in the system. Generated automatically upon token creation using UUID v4 format to ensure global uniqueness.

todo_list_user_id.description:
Reference to the user who requested the password reset.

Foreign key linking to the todo_list_users table's id column. Identifies which user account this password reset token was generated for, establishing the relationship between reset tokens and user accounts.

This field is used internally by the system to associate tokens with user accounts and enforce user-specific password reset operations. When a token is validated, the system uses this field to identify which user's password should be reset.

token.description:
Cryptographically secure random token sent in password reset email.

Unique token string generated using secure cryptographic methods. This value is sent to the user's email as part of the password reset link. Must be unique across all active tokens to prevent collisions and ensure each reset request is uniquely identifiable.

The token is validated during password reset operations to verify the authenticity of the request.

email.description:
Email address where the password reset link was sent.

Stored for validation purposes to ensure the token is used with the correct email address, providing an additional security layer. This field is checked against the user's current email during password reset to prevent token misuse.

Must be a valid email format conforming to RFC 5322 standards.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the password reset token was generated.

Records the exact moment this token was created in ISO 8601 format. Used to calculate token expiration and track the age of reset requests for security monitoring and cleanup operations.

expires_at.description:
Timestamp when this token becomes invalid.

Calculated as 1 hour after creation timestamp. The system automatically rejects password reset attempts using tokens past this expiration time, enforcing time-limited validity for security.

Expired tokens should be cleaned up from the database periodically.

used_at.description:
Timestamp when the token was successfully used to reset password.

Null for unused tokens. Once set to a timestamp, indicates the token has been consumed and cannot be reused, enforcing the single-use security requirement.

This field is critical for preventing token replay attacks.

ITodoListPasswordResetToken.description:
Password reset token entity for secure account recovery.

Represents a temporary, time-limited token sent via email when users request password resets. Each token is cryptographically secure, single-use, and expires after 1 hour to maintain strict security controls.

Tokens are created when users initiate the password reset flow through the "Forgot Password" feature. The system generates a unique token, associates it with the user's email, and sends a reset link. When users access the reset link, the system validates the token's authenticity, expiration status, and usage state before allowing password updates.

This entity supports the complete password reset lifecycle including token generation, validation, usage tracking, and cleanup of expired or used tokens.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the password reset token.

This is the primary key that uniquely identifies each password reset token record in the todo_list_password_reset_tokens table. Used for retrieving, updating, or deleting specific token records in administrative operations.

todo_list_user_id.description:
User who requested the password reset.

Foreign key reference to the todo_list_users table identifying which user account this password reset token belongs to. Essential for administrative monitoring to correlate reset requests with user accounts, investigate security incidents, and audit password reset patterns.

Allows administrators to see all reset attempts for a specific user without fetching the complete user object, maintaining efficient data transfer while providing necessary context for security operations.

token.description:
Cryptographically secure random token sent in password reset email.

Must be unique across all active tokens to prevent collisions. Used to verify password reset requests. This sensitive security credential should only be transmitted in password reset emails and must be protected from unauthorized access.

Included in administrative views for security auditing purposes, allowing administrators to verify token uniqueness and investigate potential security issues. The token value is the actual credential users receive via email to complete their password reset.

email.description:
Email address where the password reset link was sent.

Stored for validation to ensure the token is used with the correct email, providing an additional security layer. This field helps administrators verify password reset email delivery and investigate user-reported issues with reset link receipt.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the password reset token was generated.

Used to calculate token expiration (tokens expire 1 hour after creation) and for time-based security analysis. Administrators can monitor reset request patterns and identify suspicious activity by analyzing token creation timestamps.

expires_at.description:
Timestamp when this token becomes invalid.

Set to 1 hour after creation. The system rejects password reset attempts using expired tokens. Critical for security auditing to identify expired tokens requiring cleanup and to enforce time-limited password reset windows.

used_at.description:
Timestamp when the token was successfully used to reset password, or null if unused.

Null for unused tokens. Once set, the token cannot be reused, enforcing single-use security requirement. Helps administrators identify abandoned reset requests (null values) and verify successful password reset completions.

ITodoListPasswordResetToken.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary of password reset token for list views and administrative monitoring.

Provides essential token information including user association, email destination, timestamps, and usage status. Optimized for displaying multiple tokens in administrative views, security audit logs, and user account security monitoring interfaces.

Includes the user ID to enable correlation with user accounts during administrative investigations and security auditing, allowing administrators to track all reset attempts for specific users without requiring additional API calls.

Includes the actual token value for administrative security auditing purposes, enabling verification of token uniqueness and investigation of potential security issues. The token is sensitive cryptographic data that administrators need access to for security monitoring and troubleshooting password reset problems.

Minimizes data transfer while providing complete metadata necessary for administrative monitoring and security operations.

limit.description:

user_id.description:

Returns only password reset tokens associated with the specified user ID. Useful for viewing all reset attempts for a particular account during security investigations.

email.description:

Returns only tokens sent to the specified email address. Helps identify password reset requests by email when investigating delivery issues.

is_expired.description:
Filter by expiration status of password reset tokens.

When true, returns only expired tokens (expires_at in the past). When false, returns only valid unexpired tokens. Useful for cleanup operations and security auditing.

is_used.description:
Filter by usage status of password reset tokens.

When true, returns only tokens that have been used (used_at is not null). When false, returns only unused tokens. Helps identify abandoned reset requests.

created_after.description:
Filter tokens created after this timestamp.

Returns only password reset tokens with created_at after the specified date. Useful for time-range security analysis and monitoring recent reset activity.

created_before.description:
Filter tokens created before this timestamp.

Returns only password reset tokens with created_at before the specified date. Combined with created_after to define date ranges for security auditing.

ITodoListPasswordResetToken.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for querying password reset tokens.

Defines parameters for searching the todo_list_password_reset_tokens table with support for filtering by user, token status, expiration state, and creation date ranges. Enables administrative monitoring of password reset requests and security auditing.

Supports pagination through page and limit parameters to handle large result sets efficiently. Filter criteria can be combined to create complex queries such as finding all expired unused tokens for a specific user within a date range.

Used in administrative operations to monitor password reset patterns, detect potential security threats, identify tokens requiring cleanup, and investigate user-reported issues with password reset functionality.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the todo item.

Primary key that uniquely identifies each todo in the system. Generated automatically upon creation using UUID v4 format to ensure global uniqueness across all users.

ITodoListTodo.description:
Todo item entity representing user tasks and action items.

Represents individual tasks, goals, or action items created by authenticated users to track their work and personal activities. Each todo belongs to exactly one user and maintains complete data isolation between users.

Supports rich metadata including titles, descriptions, due dates, priority levels, and completion status. The status field tracks workflow progression between pending and completed states, allowing users to mark tasks as done while preserving historical records.

Implements soft deletion through the deleted_at timestamp, providing a 30-day recovery window before permanent deletion. Optional categorization allows users to organize related todos without requiring categories for basic functionality.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new todo item.

Contains only user-provided fields required or optional for todo creation. System-managed fields like id, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at are automatically generated. The user_id is derived from the authenticated user's JWT token and must not be provided in the request body.

Priority defaults to medium if not specified. Status always defaults to pending for new todos. Category is optional and can be set during creation or added later.

title.description:
Updated brief description of the task to be completed.

This field updates the primary identifier users see for each todo item. When provided, it replaces the existing title with a new concise description of the action to be taken.

Validation: Must be between 1 and 200 characters. Empty strings are not allowed as they would make the todo item unidentifiable in list views. Maximum length ensures titles remain scannable and don't overwhelm the user interface.

Usage: Commonly updated when task scope changes, when initial title was unclear, or when reprioritizing work requires more descriptive labels.

description.description:
Updated detailed notes or additional context about the todo item.

This optional field updates longer explanations, instructions, checklist items, or related information that doesn't fit in the title. When provided, it replaces the existing description entirely.

Validation: Maximum length of 2000 characters allows for substantial detail while preventing abuse. Set to null to explicitly clear existing description and remove all additional context from the todo.

Usage: Updated when task requirements change, when additional context is discovered, or when simplifying a todo by removing unnecessary details. The null value is useful for cleaning up todos that no longer need extended explanations.

due_date.description:
Updated deadline or target completion date for this todo item.

This field updates the timestamp indicating when the task should be completed. When provided, it replaces any existing due date with the new target.

Validation: Must be a valid ISO 8601 formatted date-time string. Supports both past dates (for tracking overdue items) and future dates (for upcoming deadlines). Set to null to remove the existing deadline when time constraints no longer apply.

Usage: Commonly updated when priorities shift, when original estimates were incorrect, or when external factors change project timelines. Removing due dates (null) is appropriate for tasks that transition from time-sensitive to ongoing maintenance items.

oneOf.description: Low priority level - task can wait and has minimal urgency.
Medium priority level - standard task importance requiring normal attention.
High priority level - urgent task requiring immediate attention.

priority.description:
Updated priority level indicating task urgency or importance.

This field updates the classification that helps users identify which tasks require immediate attention versus those that can wait. When provided, it replaces the existing priority with the new level.

Validation: Must be exactly one of three database-enforced values: "low", "medium", or "high". The database CHECK constraint ensures only valid priority values are accepted, preventing invalid data regardless of how updates are submitted.

Usage: Commonly updated during daily planning, when business priorities shift, when deadlines approach, or when dependencies are resolved. Changing priority helps users maintain an accurate view of their most important work.

oneOf.description: Pending status - task is not yet finished and requires completion.
Completed status - task is finished and no longer requires action.

status.description:
Updated completion status tracking workflow progression.

This field toggles the todo between incomplete and finished states. When provided, it updates the current status to reflect the new workflow position.

Validation: Must be exactly one of two database-enforced values: "pending" (task not yet finished) or "completed" (task finished). The database CHECK constraint ensures data integrity. Users can freely toggle between states as work progresses or as completed tasks need to be reopened.

Usage: Most commonly toggled when users complete tasks (pending → completed) or when completed tasks need to be reopened due to new requirements (completed → pending). This field is central to the todo workflow and is updated frequently during daily task management.

todo_list_category_id.description:
Updated category assignment for organizing related todos.

This field changes which user-defined category groups this todo with related items. When provided, it replaces any existing category reference with the new one.

Validation: Must be a valid UUID referencing an existing category that belongs to the authenticated user. Cross-user category references are rejected to maintain data isolation. Set to null to remove categorization entirely when the todo no longer fits into any organizational structure.

Usage: Updated when reorganizing todo lists, when creating new categories, or when a task's context changes. Removing categorization (null) is appropriate for standalone tasks that don't fit existing organizational schemes.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing todo item with partial modifications.

This DTO enables comprehensive updates to all mutable todo fields through a single API call. All fields are optional, allowing granular partial updates where only specified fields are modified while others remain unchanged. The system automatically updates the updated_at timestamp to reflect the modification time.

Ownership and System Fields: The todo's ownership (user_id) is immutable and cannot be changed through updates. System-managed fields including id, created_at, and deleted_at are protected and cannot be modified. Users can only update todos they own as enforced by JWT-based authorization verification.

Validation: All field-level constraints from creation apply to updates. The target todo must exist, must not be soft-deleted, and must be owned by the authenticated user. Category references must exist and belong to the user. Priority and status values are database-enforced through CHECK constraints.

Usage Context: Supports common todo management workflows including title edits, description updates, deadline adjustments, priority changes, completion toggles, and category reassignments. Enables both single-field updates (e.g., just toggling status) and multi-field updates (e.g., changing title, priority, and due date simultaneously).

id.description:
Unique identifier for this category.

UUID v4 format that serves as the primary key uniquely identifying each category in the system. Generated automatically upon category creation to ensure global uniqueness across all users.

This identifier is used for referencing the category in API endpoints (e.g., /categories/{categoryId}), establishing foreign key relationships with todo items via their todo_list_category_id field, and maintaining referential integrity throughout the application.

Usage: Embedded in todo items to indicate category membership, used in URL paths for category-specific operations, and referenced in update operations to assign or change todo categorization.

name.description:
Category display name for user interface presentation.

The user-visible category label such as "Work", "Personal", "Shopping", or "Health" that appears in dropdowns, list views, and todo item displays. This is the primary human-readable identifier for the category.

Validation: Maximum length of 50 characters ensures category names remain concise and scannable in UI elements. Must be unique within the user's category list to prevent confusion and maintain clear organizational structure.

Relationship: Each user maintains their own independent category namespace, allowing different users to have categories with the same name without conflict. Category names help users quickly identify and filter todos by thematic groupings.

created_at.description:
Category creation timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

Indicates when this category was originally created by the user. Automatically set by the system upon creation and never modified thereafter, providing a stable audit trail.

Usage: Used for sorting categories chronologically in list views (e.g., showing newest categories first), displaying category age in management interfaces, and tracking when organizational structures were established.

Format: Follows ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., "2024-01-15T14:30:00Z") ensuring consistent time representation across different client timezones and enabling proper temporal sorting.

ITodoListCategory.ISummary.description:
Lightweight category summary optimized for list views and embedded references.

This optimized DTO variant contains only essential category information needed for displaying categories in dropdown menus, todo item references, and category list views. Excludes heavyweight metadata to improve performance when loading multiple categories or embedding category references within todo items.

Optimization Strategy: Omits updated_at timestamp and owner information (user_id) to minimize payload size. These fields are available in the full category detail DTO but are unnecessary for most display contexts where categories appear.

Usage Contexts: Used when embedding category information within todo items (ITodoListTodo.category field), populating category selection dropdowns during todo creation/updates, displaying category lists in management interfaces, and providing category context in search results.

Performance Benefits: Smaller payload size enables faster API responses when returning lists of todos (each containing a category reference) or when loading category dropdown options. Reduces bandwidth consumption and improves client-side rendering speed.

Category names must be unique per user to prevent organizational confusion. The system supports user-specific categories, meaning each user maintains their own category list independent of other users.
